items.desc: NATO chief Mark Rutte said Monday the alliance would defend against threats in space when asked about German media reports that Russia may be preparing to launch a nuclear-armed satellite. Speaking with FRANCE 24's Jennie Shin, Dafydd Townley, Senior Teaching Fellow in International Security at the University of Portsmouth, says that the alleged plan would be "foolhardy because the impact would be indiscriminate, they wouldn't be able to choose only Western or non-Russian satellites".

items.title: The Bukele method: will Salvadoran leader's strong-arm tactics work for Haiti?
items.desc: Haitians are hailing the Bukele method. Citizens of the Americas’ poorest nation cheering the Salvadoran president’s ’shoot first, ask questions later’ method of dealing with the gangs that have overrun their country the past six years. Can the police force deployed actually restore law and order? We’ll ask about the latest in a decades-long list of efforts by the international community to support Haiti.

items.title: Senegal AFCON ruling 'good in the books of sports law', expert says
items.desc: Speaking with FRANCE 24's Jennie Shin, sports presenter and journalist Thando Sibiya explains that the decision by the Court of Arbitration for Sport to reinstate Senegal as ⁠winner of ​the 2025 Africa Cup of Nations "from a jurisprudence perspective or creating precedent, it is going to be good in the books of sports law, because if every single decision of a referee is taken to a court of law all the time, it really tampers with the quality, governance and legitimacy of the game".

items.title: Senegal regain AFCON title on appeal at Morocco's expense
items.desc: Senegal on Tuesday regained their Africa Cup of Nations title after winning an appeal at the Court of Arbitration for Sport (CAS) against the decision by the Confederation of African Football to declare Morocco the winners following a chaotic final in January. CAS said in a statement it had "upheld the appeal by the Senegalese Football Federation (FSF) against the Confederation of African Football (CAF) and the Royal Moroccan Football Federation (FRMF)" by a "unanimous decision". FRANCE 24's Emerald Maxwell reports.

items.title: Car bomb destroys buildings in central Colombian city
items.desc: A car bomb detonated in the central Colombian city of Villavicencio on Monday, destroying a local governor's office and surrounding buildings, President Abelardo de la Espriella said. The right-wing leader has conducted a major crackdown on the country's drug trade, in response to left-wing FARC rebels who have stepped up attacks over the past two years. FRANCE 24's Daniel Whittington reports.

items.title: Russian losses on Ukrainian front top 700,000 including missing
items.desc: New analysis of leaked Russian government data suggests more than 700,000 Russian soldiers have died in the war against Ukraine. Independent Russian media outlets have updated their estimates of Moscow's military casualties, including soldiers missing on the frontline, after Belarusian and Ukrainian hackers obtained figures from the Russian statistics agency. FRANCE 24's Carys Garland explains.

items.title: Gunmen hold 25 people hostage at supermarket in Colombia's Cartagena
items.desc: Armed robbers took 25 people hostage at a supermarket in Colombia’s tourist city of Cartagena on Tuesday, prompting a major police operation and a temporary suspension of incoming flights, authorities said. Landings at Rafael Nunez International Airport resumed after the military used a runway during the operation.

items.title: Russia's war on Ukraine: 'Both sides are prepared to operate outside of the conflict zone'
items.desc: Charli James is pleased to welcome Gavin Hall, Teaching Fellow in Political Science, and International Security at the University of Strathclyde. Hall examines recent Russian and Ukrainian operations beyond the main conflict zone, the conditions necessary for a negotiated settlement and the implications of diminishing direct US military support for Ukraine. “Both sides are prepared to operate beyond the main battleground and outside of the conflict zone,” he explains. Hall discusses why both sides want to negotiate from a position of strength and the conditions under which a “mutually hurting stalemate” could lead to a negotiated settlement.

items.title: Yemen’s army says Houthi fighters closing in on government stronghold of Aden
items.desc: Yemen's military on Tuesday said that Houthi fighters were closing in on the internationally recognised government's stronghold of Aden from about 60km (40 miles) away and vowed to repel any assault. A military spokesman said defences were prepared following Houthi advances and government pullbacks near the Red Sea.

items.title: France's ex-president Nicolas Sarkozy, wife Carla Bruni to stand trial for alleged witness tampering
items.desc: France's former president Nicolas Sarkozy and his wife, singer Carla Bruni-Sarkozy, are set to be tried in 2027 on charges of "criminal conspiracy with intent to commit fraud" as well as benefitting from witness tampering. The new charges are related to the Sarkozy couple's actions during the case examining illegal campaign funding from Libyan strongman Muammar Gaddafi over which Sarkozy was imprisoned last year.

items.title: 'We are ready to facilitate removal of Netanyahu': Head of Israel's Arab
items.desc: In an interview with FRANCE 24, the head of the Arab-majority Joint List said his political alliance is prepared to play a decisive role in bringing down Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's government following the recent election. "We are ready to facilitate the removal of Netanyahu" from power, Yousef Jabareen said, signalling a willingness to explore political alliances beyond traditional divisions in Israeli politics.

items.title: Senegal reinstated as 2025 Africa Cup of Nations winners
items.desc: Senegal ​were reinstated as 2025 Africa Cup of Nations winners ​on Tuesday after the Court of Arbitration for Sport upheld their appeal against being stripped of the title. Senegal contested the ​Confederation ‌of African Football's decision to declare ⁠Morocco champions, despite Senegal beating the hosts 1-0 after extra time in ‌January's final in Rabat. Morocco announced that it would “pursue all necessary legal procedures” in response to the decision.

items.title: 'Tis the season to be green: Can the Christmas holidays be a present for the planet?
items.desc: With the holiday season just around the corner, we take a look at its environmental impact. We discuss how to make Christmas a little greener as consumers, whether plastic trees or natural ones are better for the planet, and what small steps we can all take to reduce our carbon footprint during the festivities.

items.title: French police officer who shot teenager to face murder trial
items.desc: A French police officer will stand trial for murder in the killing of a teenager in 2023 that sparked violent protests across the country, the Versailles appeals court said on Tuesday. Nahel Merzouk, 17, was shot in the Paris suburb of Nanterre after he failed to comply with an order to stop his car.

items.title: Leaked data suggests 500,000 Russian soldiers killed since start of Ukraine invasion
items.desc: More than 500,000 Russian soldiers have been killed in the war with Ukraine, according to an estimate by a number of media organisations. The figures are based on a huge dataset that was hacked from Russia’s state statistics agency Rosstat by Belarusian activist group Cyber Partisans and a Ukrainian hacker group, Silent Crow. Two independent Russian news outlets Meduza and Mediazona say the death toll may rise to more than 700,000 once missing soldiers are included.

items.title: Burnham's EU reset brings back Brexit debate
items.desc: UK Prime Minister Andy Burnham accused predecessors who have warned him against reigniting the Brexit debate of being "stuck in the past", as he trumpeted his EU reset deal on Monday. Burnham has in recent weeks smashed a consensus that Britain's acrimonious departure from the European Union was done and dusted, floating the possibility that Britain could apply to rejoin. Clovis Casali takes a closer look.

items.title: 'Nina Roza' director: 'I was inspired by a real case of a child painter prodigy'
items.desc: The director of a film nominated by Canada for next year's Oscars has told FRANCE 24 she was inspired by stories of a child painter prodigy, as well as the idea of identity and what you leave behind when you change countries. The film "Nina Roza" tells the story of a Bulgarian man who leaves his homeland with his daughter and sets himself up as an art curator in Canada.

items.title: UK’s Burnham on a mission to build public support EU reset
items.desc: While he insists it would be unthinkable to rejoin the bloc without another referendum, British PM Andy Burnham has nevertheless reopened the debate over Brexit. After striking a deal that brings the UK and the EU closer on issues including food export control standards, youth mobility and carbon emissions, he's set to discuss the future of the relationship with Brussels in the coming weeks and will present the results of the talks in December. It comes despite criticism from a host of former Conservative prime ministers.

items.title: The French mayors refusing to back presidential candidates
items.desc: Tuesday marks the opening in Paris of the 108th Congress of French Mayors, where the presidential race is a contentious issue. Candidates need 500 mayor endorsements to run, yet nearly half of mayors this year say they refuse to endorse anyone. France 2 and Caitlin Brown have more.

items.title: France's femicide orphans: The invisible victims of violence against women
items.desc: In France, 111 women were killed by their current or ex-partners in 2025 alone, leaving behind dozens of children. How can they rebuild their lives without their mother? How can they seek help? In this episode of France in Focus, we meet Cloé and Eva-Louise, whose world collapsed when their father brutally murdered their mother. FRANCE 24's Natacha Vesnitch, Olivia Bizot, Clément Di Roma and Aurore Cloé Dupuis report.

items.title: 【前方视野】1.5摄氏度临界点逼近：中国如何回答气候变化时代的转型之问
